title: Box Plots, Outliers and Standard Deviation
seo_title: Algebra 1 Statistics Worksheets: Box Plots, IQR, Outliers and Standard Deviation (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 1 statistics worksheets (S-ID.A.1–3): five-number summary and IQR, reading box plots, outliers with the 1.5 × IQR rule, standard deviation and comparing distributions by shape, center and spread. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Median and IQR resist outliers; mean and standard deviation suit symmetric data.
key_sub: IQR = Q3 − Q1. Outliers lie more than 1.5 × IQR beyond the box.
body_html:
How it works

The five-number summary is the minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Order the data first; Q1 and Q3 are the medians of the lower and upper halves. A box plot draws these five numbers. The IQR = Q3 − Q1 is the spread of the middle half.

An outlier is below Q1 − 1.5 × IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 × IQR. Outliers pull the mean but hardly move the median.

The standard deviation measures how far values typically are from the mean. Adding a constant to every value does not change it; multiplying every value by k multiplies it by k.

Example

Find the five-number summary of 3, 7, 8, 5, 12, 14, 21, 13, 18.

Order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 18, 21.

Lower half 3, 5, 7, 8 → Q1 = 6. Upper half 13, 14, 18, 21 → Q3 = 16.

Answer: 3, 6, 12, 16, 21

Example

Is 40 an outlier if Q1 = 6 and Q3 = 16?

IQR = 10.

Upper fence = 16 + 15 = 31.

Answer: Yes, 40 > 31

Common mistakes

  • Finding the median or quartiles without ordering the data first.
  • Giving the range (max − min) when asked for the IQR (Q3 − Q1).
  • Reading the ends of the whiskers as the quartiles. The quartiles are the edges of the box.
  • Thinking that adding the same number to every value changes the spread.

faq.a: The minimum, first quartile (Q1), median, third quartile (Q3) and maximum of a data set. A box plot shows all five.
Find IQR = Q3 − Q1. Any value below Q1 − 1.5 × IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 × IQR is an outlier.
How spread out the data is around the mean. A small standard deviation means the values are close to the mean.

faq.q: When should I use the median instead of the mean?
faq.a: When the data is skewed or has outliers. The median is not pulled by extreme values.

items.q: A data set is skewed right (a long tail of high values). Which is usually larger?
items.e: The high values pull the mean up: the mean is larger.

items.q: Which measures of center and spread are best for a skewed data set with outliers?
items.e: The median and IQR are not affected much by outliers: median and IQR.

items.q: Which measures are best for a symmetric data set with no outliers?
items.e: For symmetric data the mean and standard deviation describe it well.

items.q: Class A's test scores have mean 78 and SD 4. Class B's have mean 78 and SD 12. What does this tell you?
c: Class B's scores are more spread out
items.e: Same center, but a larger SD means more spread.

items.q: Two box plots have the same median, but box A is twice as wide as box B. What does this mean?
c: The middle half of A is more spread out
items.e: The box width is the IQR: A's middle half is more spread out.

items.q: In a normal (bell-shaped) distribution, about what percent of data is within 1 standard deviation of the mean?
items.e: The 68–95–99.7 rule: about 68% within 1 SD.

items.q: Heights of adult women have mean 64 in. and SD 2.5 in. About 95% of women are between which heights?
items.e: 95% is within 2 SD: 64 ± 5 → 59 to 69 in.

items.q: Which graph best shows the five-number summary?
items.e: A box plot shows the minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum.

items.q: Which graph best shows the shape of a large data set?
items.e: A histogram shows how the data is distributed (peaks, skew and gaps).

items.q: A store's daily sales: mean $2,400, median $1,900. What shape is the distribution likely to be?
items.e: The mean is greater than the median, so a few very high days pull it up: skewed right.

items.q: A teacher adds 5 points to every test score. What happens to the median and IQR?
c: The median stays the same; the IQR goes up 5
The median goes up 5; the IQR stays the same
items.e: Adding a constant shifts the center but not the spread.

items.q: Which data set has the larger IQR: A: Q1 = 20, Q3 = 35; B: Q1 = 15, Q3 = 25?
The ages at a children's party are 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8 and one adult aged 38. Which measure of center describes a typical age best?
items.e: The adult is an outlier that pulls the mean up to 10.5; the median 7 is more typical.

items.q: What does a standard deviation of 0 mean?
c: All the values are the same
items.e: No value is away from the mean: all the values are the same.

items.q: Two classes have these quiz scores. Class A: median 8, IQR 2. Class B: median 7, IQR 5. Which statement is true?
c: Class A scored higher and more consistently
items.e: Higher median and smaller IQR: Class A scored higher and more consistently.

items.q: Which is NOT part of the five-number summary?
items.e: The five-number summary is min, Q1, median, Q3 and max. The mean is not part of it.

items.q: A data set is skewed left. Which is true?
c: The mean is usually greater than the median
The mean is usually less than the median
items.e: A tail of low values pulls the mean down: mean < median.

items.q: A box plot's left whisker is much longer than its right whisker. What shape is the data?
items.e: The long tail is on the low (left) side: skewed left.

items.q: Which change would increase the standard deviation of 10, 12, 14, 16, 18?
items.e: Moving a value far from the mean increases the spread: replace 18 with 30.

items.q: Battery A lasts a mean of 10 h with SD 0.5 h. Battery B lasts a mean of 10.5 h with SD 3 h. Which is more reliable?
items.e: Battery A's times vary much less: battery A is more reliable, even though B's mean is a bit higher.
